_note: Finished leather goods made by the leatherworker from the tanner's leather (Complaints/612): shoes, a draught animal's harness and a sword scabbard. Every mass, hour count and life is a recalled or estimated figure, marked in each yield_basis.

shoes_pair.basis: per pair of stitched leather shoes
shoes_pair.yield_basis: A pair of hand-stitched leather shoes or boots uses a bit under a kilogram of finished leather for sole, upper and thongs (recalled from museum finds of Roman and medieval shoes, not opened; conf D), cut and sewn by a leatherworker in about a working day (author's estimate, conf D). Thread and nails are a few grams and are left out. CLOTHING: the pair satisfies the clothing need at the factor leather_kg already carries per kilogram of leather it holds (data/world/needs.json), so a worked pair is worth its leather and no more until a source gives cover and warmth of footwear separately; a labelled placeholder, retire with a need for footwear.

harness_set.basis: per set of leather harness for one draught animal: collar pad, traces, reins, girth and straps
harness_set.yield_basis: Straps, traces and reins for one animal run to some eight kilograms of heavy leather and a thirty-hour stitching job for a saddler (author's estimate from the size of the pieces, conf D; metal fittings and the wooden collar or yoke are left out). It is a capital good of a draught animal: it is bought by whoever works the animal, so it has no household need of its own.

scabbard_leather.basis: per leather-covered scabbard and belt for one sword or dagger
scabbard_leather.yield_basis: A leather sheath with its belt uses some four tenths of a kilogram of leather and a few hours of cutting, wetting, moulding and stitching (author's estimate, conf D). It is the soldier's kit, bought by whoever arms a soldier, and carries no household need of its own.
